messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] kvcache.oom_count spike (hosted-runtime-us-west-2). 80% of serving pods reporting OOMs in last 60s. Possible runaway prefetch / long prompt amplification. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-oom — paging oncall.

carla_oncall: I'm oncall and looking. seeing a ton of sessions with massive context prefixes. hitting KVAllocation failures. paging infra for emergency throttle.

liz.sre: @carla_oncall any customer-facing errors/rates? are we returning 5xx or just slow/queued?

carla_oncall: quick metrics: error rate (500s) up ~1.8% across hosted, p95 latencies spiked 400ms -> 2.1s for generation start. spikes align with heavy prefetch windows. list of impacted tenants: alpha-corp, beta-chat, some free-tier customers.

andre.eng: can you paste the log snippets? suspect continuous-batching + large prefetch window causing KV map growth + eviction thrash.

carla_oncall: logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] serving-17 ERR: OOM allocating 1.2G KV segment for session sess_7f9ab... model=redwy-large
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] kvcache-manager WARN: prefetch_window=25000 tokens for model redwy-large, candidate_count=12 -> growth spike
[2026-03-15T09:12:12Z] batching-agent INFO: batch_window_ms=20, continuous_batching=true, active_batches=230
```

carla_oncall: rolling a config hotfix to throttle prefetch and reduce batch window. patched the hosted runtime config to soft-disable prefetch until we stabilize.

andre.eng: agreed plan: 1) disable prefetch globally for hosted runtime region, 2) reduce batch_window_ms to 8, 3) kick eviction sweep, 4) add temporary soft cap on KV-index entries per session. Apply patch and watch.

carla_oncall: applying patch now:
```
infractl apply --env=hosted-usw2 --patch=kvcache-prefetch-throttle-20260315.json
# patch contents:
{
  "prefetch_enabled": false,
  "prefetch_max_tokens": 1024,
  "batch_window_ms": 8,
  "kv_soft_cap_per_session": 2000
}
```

deploy-bot: Patch applied to hosted-usw2 config (canary 3 pods) — id: canary-20260315-01. Monitoring rollout.

carla_oncall: canary looks good so far, no new OOMs in canary pods for last 30s. beginning gradual rollout.

andre.eng: also bumping eviction aggressiveness: running
```
python tools/evict_sweep.py --region=us-west-2 --aggression=high --dryrun=false
```

liz.sre: customer impact update: approx 2.1k requests failed with 5xx during spike window (09:10:40 - 09:13:20 UTC). alpha-corp experienced degraded throughput for 90s. CS notified. SLA risk low but visible.

customer-success-amy: I'm messaging alpha-corp and beta-chat now with an incident note and ETA for follow-up. keeping them informed.

deploy-bot: rollout completed to 100% hosted-usw2. No new OOMs observed in 5m window post-rollout.

carla_oncall: metrics: kvcache.oom_count dropped to baseline, error rate back to normal (~0.2%). p95 generation start back to 420ms.

andre.eng: immediate mitigations worked. next steps: - instrument prefix amplification detection (alert) - implement adaptive prefetch cap tied to session token length - add per-session KV hard cap in runtime - run full postmortem once stable.

jordan_pd: customer impact question: do we need credits or follow-up engineering work for alpha-corp? Amy, what are they asking?

customer-success-amy: alpha-corp asked for a short summary and assurance it's fixed; no credit request yet. I'll gather logs for their SLA contact.

carla_oncall: handing off to @andre.eng for continued investigation and postmortem. I'm switching to secondary for meeting. Contact list: @andre.eng (owner), @liz.sre (sre reviewer), @customer-success-amy (customer comms).

andre.eng: taking over. next immediate action items assigned: 1) correlate long-prompt sessions with prefetch triggers and create a dashboard (assigned to me), 2) PR to add per-session KV hard cap and config guardrails (estimate 2d), 3) add alert for kvcache.prefix_amplification ratio > 3x baseline (ops ticket).

carla_oncall: thanks team. leaving note: if we re-enable prefetch, do it behind adaptive cap and only after evictions/soft-caps are live.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned -> mitigation applied. Severity: Sev-2 (service impact contained). Pager cleared for oncall. Postmortem requested.

andre.eng: I'll post an initial incident timeline and share in #incidents after we validate traces.

customer-success-amy: I'll send the interim customer message in 15m and offer a follow-up call if they want.

liz.sre: leaving a quick ops tip for postmortem: include sequence of kernel selections under stress — we saw memory-heavy kernel being chosen for long context model.

carla_oncall: end of thread handoff: @andre.eng owns post-incident follow-through. closing oncall shift.
